question:
(i) A photon emitted by an atom has energy $4.0\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}$. Calculate its frequency. Take $h=6.63\times10^{-34}\,\text{J s}$.
(ii) Explain why emitted frequencies in an atomic spectrum are discrete.

options.A:
(i) $\nu=\dfrac{h}{E}=1.66\times10^{-15}\,\text{Hz}$.
(ii) Atomic frequencies are discrete because energy levels are continuous.
options.B:
(i) $\nu=6.03\times10^{13}\,\text{Hz}$.
(ii) Frequencies are discrete because electrons can possess every possible energy.
options.C:
(i) $\nu=Eh=2.65\times10^{-52}\,\text{Hz}$.
(ii) Atomic spectra are discrete because frequency does not depend on energy differences.
options.D:
(i) $\nu=\dfrac{E}{h}=\dfrac{4.0\times10^{-19}}{6.63\times10^{-34}}=6.03\times10^{14}\,\text{Hz}$.
(ii) Atoms have discrete levels; transitions satisfy $h\nu=E_i-E_f$, so only definite frequencies are emitted.
